questions.question: A 2.0 cm object is 10 cm from a diverging lens (f = -15 cm). Image distance is closest to:
questions.fastStrategy: For diverging, expect negative image inside f; here ~-6 cm.

questions.question: Speed of sound in a string with tension 200 N and linear density 0.020 kg/m is:
A 600 nm light passes through a 0.40 mm double slit onto a screen 2.0 m away. Fringe spacing is:
A wave on a string reflects from a free end. The reflected pulse is:
questions.explanation: Free end imposes an antinode; reflection is upright (no inversion).

questions.question: Light in glass (n=1.50) enters water (n=1.33) at 50° to the normal. Refraction angle is closest to:
questions.explanation: sinθ2 = (n1/n2) sinθ1 = (1.50/1.33)×sin50 ≈ 0.866 → θ2 ≈ 60°. Closest option is 62°.
questions.fastStrategy: Going to lower n bends away; expect >50°, about 60°.

questions.question: A 40 W source emits uniformly. Intensity at 5.0 m is:
In an organ pipe open at both ends of length 0.85 m, fundamental frequency (v=340 m/s) is:
questions.explanation: For open-open, f1 = v/(2L) = 340 / 1.70 ≈ 200 Hz.

questions.question: Phase difference corresponding to a path difference of one wavelength is:
questions.explanation: One full wavelength corresponds to 2π radians of phase.

questions.question: A 150 Hz sound reflects from a moving wall and returns at 156 Hz. Wall speed toward source is closest to: (v=340 m/s)
questions.explanation: Two Doppler shifts: f' = f (v+vw)/(v-vw). Let r = 156/150 = 1.04 = (v+vw)/(v-vw). Solve: r(v - vw) = v + vw → rv - r vw = v + vw → (r+1)vw = (r-1)v → vw = (0.04/2.04)·340 ≈ 6.7 m/s.

questions.question: A 450 nm light enters sapphire (n=1.77). Its wavelength inside is:
questions.explanation: Wavelength in medium λ' = λ/n = 450/1.77 ≈ 254 nm.

questions.question: A laser (λ=650 nm) passes through a 0.20 mm single slit. Central maximum angular width (min-to-min) is approximately:
questions.explanation: Single-slit minima at sinθ = mλ/a. For first minima ±1: sinθ = λ/a = 650e-9/2e-4 = 3.25e-3 → θ ≈ 0.186°. Full width ≈ 2θ ≈ 0.37°.

questions.question: For a 1.0 m organ pipe closed at one end, first overtone frequency (v=340 m/s) is:
questions.explanation: Closed pipe supports odd harmonics. Fundamental f1 = v/(4L) = 340/4 = 85 Hz. First overtone is 3f1 = 255 Hz.

questions.question: A wave has amplitude doubled while frequency unchanged. Its power transmission becomes:
questions.explanation: Power/intensity ∝ amplitude^2. Doubling amplitude quadruples power.

questions.question: An EM wave has electric field amplitude 6.0 V/m in vacuum. Magnetic field amplitude is:
questions.explanation: In vacuum, E = cB ⇒ B = E/c = 6 / (3e8) = 2.0×10^-8 T.

questions.question: A 0.60 m string has mass 12 g. If tension is 48 N, the fundamental frequency is:
questions.explanation: Linear density μ = 0.012/0.60 = 0.020 kg/m. Wave speed v = sqrt(T/μ) = sqrt(48/0.02) = sqrt(2400) ≈ 49 m/s. f1 = v/(2L) ≈ 49/1.2 ≈ 41 Hz → closest 50 Hz.

questions.question: A radar uses 3.0 cm wavelength. Its frequency is:
A 100 Hz sound in air (v=340 m/s) enters water (v=1500 m/s). Its frequency in water is:
questions.explanation: Frequency stays the same across media; wavelength changes.
questions.fastStrategy: Frequency is source-set; medium changes speed/λ only.

questions.question: A 250 W lamp radiates 5% of its power as visible light. Visible output in watts is:
questions.fastStrategy: Ten percent is 25; half that is 12.5.

questions.question: A 400 Hz source approaches a stationary observer at 30 m/s (v=340 m/s). Observed frequency is closest to:
questions.explanation: Moving source: f' = f v/(v - vs) = 400×(340/310) ≈ 400×1.097 ≈ 439 Hz (closest 436 Hz).

questions.question: Two polarizers at 90° stop all light. If a third is placed between them at 45° to each, transmitted fraction of initial unpolarized light is:
questions.explanation: First polarizer passes 50%. Second at 45° passes cos^2 45 = 0.5 of that → 25%. Third (90° to first, 45° to second) passes another 0.5 → 12.5% overall.
steps: Third at 90° from first (45° from second): ×0.5

questions.question: A sonar ping at 20 kHz reflects from a submarine returning in 0.80 s in seawater (v=1500 m/s). Range to submarine is:
questions.explanation: Round-trip time 0.80 s → one-way 0.40 s. Distance = v t = 1500×0.40 = 600 m.

questions.question: If a pipe length is doubled (open-open), the fundamental frequency becomes:
questions.explanation: For open-open, f1 ∝ 1/L. Doubling length halves the fundamental frequency.
questions.fastStrategy: Longer pipe → lower pitch; doubling length halves f.

questions.question: Ultraviolet has higher frequency than visible mainly because it has:
questions.explanation: In vacuum all EM waves have same speed; higher frequency means shorter wavelength (thus higher photon energy).
questions.fastStrategy: Higher f ↔ shorter λ; c constant.

questions.question: Two sine waves of equal amplitude and 180° phase difference combine. Resulting amplitude is:
questions.explanation: Equal amplitudes opposite phase cancel completely, yielding zero resultant.

questions.question: A 0.10 m diameter circular opening produces a diffraction pattern with first minimum at 3.6 mrad using 550 nm light. Aperture diameter by small-angle formula d ≈ 1.22 λ/θ is closest to:
A circular aperture has first dark ring at angle 6.7 μrad using 550 nm light. Using d ≈ 1.22 λ/θ, the aperture diameter is closest to:
